volume_units: lots (Sina shares / 100, as akshare's a_share loader serves them)

columns.hfq: trade_date,adj_factor, one row per bar in the window (Sina hfq-factor forward-filled)
columns.qfq: trade_date,open,high,low,close,volume (additive levels synthesized from the factor steps)

how_to_load: pd.read_csv(path, parse_dates=["trade_date"]).set_index("trade_date") for raw/qfq; the hfq frame keeps trade_date as a column, which is the (trade_date, adj_factor) shape cn_adjust.apply_qfq expects
dtype_notes: trade_date is datetime64 on both sides here; Sina's raw daily frame carries a date object and its factor table a datetime64, so both were normalized through the loader before writing

Sina's published hfq-factor table is reversed, string-typed, always 33 rows (window params ignored) and carries a 1900-01-01 sentinel row; loader._sina_factor sorts, casts and forward-fills it onto the window, which is what adj_factor holds here
Sina's adj_factor is a rising cumulative multiplier; brief Step 3's helper detects downward steps, so it is fed the exact divisor 1/adj_factor (g_next/g_prev == f_prev/f_next)
reading_notes: offset_distinct is the exact-float count of qfq.close - raw.close (brief Step 1's formula) and counts last-ulp cancellation noise, so it is above plateau_spans (the 1e-6 grouped plateau count); the on-disk pair is offset_distinct_on_disk / plateau_spans_on_disk. Assert plateaus, not exact float counts - the CSV text round trip moves the first number, not the second; on the refusal symbol both plateau keys are renamed pre_refusal_* on purpose - production _plateau_spans returns None there, so pre_refusal_plateau_spans=5 and pre_refusal_span_lengths=[85, 75, 97, 143, 1] is the 1e-6 grouping BEFORE that refusal (re-measured from the committed CSVs), not a span count production reached; on the three convertibles the two definitions coincide (4/5/5, production list equals the pre-grouping list), which is why this manifest never had to say which one it meant until a refusal appeared - iterating plateau keys across symbols must branch on bucket; the metric names plateau_spans / plateau_lengths / plateau_spans_on_disk stay present on the refusal symbol with a null value (production returned None there, so no span list exists), and every symbol now carries plateau_spans_production_returns_none saying which definition its plateau_spans points at (false on the three convertibles, true on the refusal)
pandas' default read_csv float parser is not bit-exact (csv_max_abs_gap_vs_capture is 1e-15 to 1e-13 on the levels); pass float_precision='round_trip' when the bits must match the capture

qfq.volume equals raw.volume by design: an additive vendor frame does not move volume, and it is the converter that divides it by the cumulative ratio; the mandated reverse check cannot see this column at all (it reads only qfq.close - raw.close and rebuilds volume from raw / ratio), so volume_identical_to_raw_on_disk is the face that falsifies a corrupt volume in _qfq.csv, and ohlc_offset_identity_max_abs is the matching face for open/high/low - see reverse_check_coverage
no symbol here is a 送转 window: on the derived path a bonus issue would be re-encoded as a cash plateau, so the converter's price-drift refusal signature cannot appear (see derived_path_limitation)

two residual faces, about five orders apart, and they are not interchangeable: reverse_check_max_rel / disk_reverse_check_max_rel are LEVEL face (600519.SH close column: 1.9273e-16 relative), while return_reverse_check_max_rel is the RETURN face (pct_change of each lane's close) that the cross-implementation return assertion pins. Measured cause on 600519.SH 2025-07-16: the two lanes' close levels differ by 2.27373675443232059e-13 at their worst bar, differencing cancels nearly all of that and leaves 2.22044604925031308e-16 of absolute return gap, and the relative residual divides THAT by the same bar's own return magnitude 2.12615166548246748e-05 (a near-flat day, 2.1262e-05) instead of by the price level: 2.22044604925031308e-16 / 2.12615166548246748e-05 = 1.04434979183220599e-11. Largest return face over the three convertibles: 1.04434979183220599e-11 (600519.SH, 2025-07-16). The level-face keys are 48425.7x (600519.SH) / 1081.8x (000001.SZ) / 767.7x (601398.SH) tighter, so pinning a level number for a return assertion goes red on the committed data as it stands. Both faces still measure agreement between two encodings of one corporate-action history (see derived_path_limitation) - neither is a second vendor's measurement, and no reading here licenses that wording

return_reverse_check_max_rel is read with pandas' DEFAULT read_csv float parser, the face the on-disk loader uses; return_reverse_check_max_rel_round_trip repeats it with float_precision='round_trip' (the capture's own bits). They agree exactly on 600519.SH and 601398.SH; on 000001.SZ parse noise moves the worst bar (2.63122856836137614e-13 at 2025-03-13 default vs 1.23123733430946016e-13 at 2026-04-13 round_trip), so part of that reading is parsing rather than conversion. Assert the default-parser key - it is the larger or equal one on all three symbols, and its max over the three is what REL_TOL must sit above. The round_trip re-read is the capture-bits face and is corroborated by that: it reproduces the committed capture-side reverse_check_max_rel bit-for-bit (600519.SH 2.15660308520428738e-16 / 000001.SZ 2.21630966570611475e-16 / 601398.SH 2.26465081303560163e-16)

ohlc_offset_identity_max_abs is the NON-close invariant: an additive encoding shifts the four price columns by one and the same offset, so (qfq[c] - raw[c]) - (qfq.close - raw.close) is 0 by construction. Off disk it is not bit-exact under the default parser - on 600519.SH only open 379 / high 355 / low 373 of 424 bars land on exactly 0.0 and the rest are one ulp of the price level apart (2.27373675443232059e-13); under float_precision='round_trip' it is 600519.SH 0.00000000000000000e+00 / 000001.SZ 0.00000000000000000e+00 / 601398.SH 8.88178419700125232e-16. Assert it as <= the recorded value, never == 0.0, or the CSV round trip alone goes red
